on_success.evidence: Successful Save: It moves 5 feet to a space of its choice that is not closer to you, if it can.

TAL_AXES_LAW_OF_THE_FALLING_TREE.why: "When you knock a creature Prone, reduce a creature to 0 HP, destroy a significant object, or suppress a barrier panel with an Axes talent, you may spend 1 CP, 1 Stamina, or expend Martial Focus. Choose one creature within 10 feet of the fallen target or broken object. That creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failed Save: It falls Prone or is pushed 10 feet away from the fall. Successful Save: It moves 5 feet to a space of its choice that is not closer to you, if it can." The save and both outcome branches run at the moment of the fall (combat/ext/axes_falling_tree.py). "Reduce to 0 HP" is a change of state, so it needs the creature to have been above 0 and to be at 0 now. The push is away from the fall itself rather than away from the wielder, and the withdrawal is the creature's own move, paid from its own movement allowance: "if it can" is that allowance, so a creature that has already spent its movement stays where it is. Suppressing a barrier panel has no suppression record on this table and stays with the GM.
